# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Since you cannot speak, please gesture a single number using finger count for the wire to cut: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3. Deaf will relay it to me in words.

Blind's request reveals a misunderstanding — Blind thinks I can gesture to them, but I can only gesture to Deaf (Deaf is the one who sees). Blind cannot see gestures at all. However, Blind's plan actually works if reinterpreted correctly: I gesture a number to Deaf, Deaf sees it and then speaks that number to Blind. That's a valid relay chain using channels that actually exist.

But wait — I don't know the wire position number (1, 2, or 3) at all. I only know the color mapping table (flashes → color). I never learned position numbers, and I have no way to observe the bomb myself. Only Deaf can see the bomb and count flashes/colors and positions.

So the correct flow is: Deaf observes flashes + wire positions/colors on the bomb, Deaf uses my table (already sent) to determine the correct color, and Deaf must identify which position number corresponds to that color, then Deaf must speak that number to Blind directly (since Deaf can speak).

I have no additional info to contribute now. I should clarify to Deaf that they should be the one relaying the final numeric answer verbally to Blind, since I have no wire-position data at all.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🖐"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please confirm with a single gesture: thumbs up means wire 1 is correct to cut, thumbs down means it is not. I will ask about each wire one at a time starting with wire 1.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind is trying to get confirmation from me about wire numbers, but I have zero information about wire positions — I only have the flash-count-to-color table. I cannot confirm or deny anything about "wire 1" since I don't know what color wire 1 is. Only Deaf knows the colors/positions on the actual bomb.

Deaf just gestured 👍 to me — likely acknowledging receipt of my table, or confirming they understand the plan to relay the color themselves. This suggests Deaf is on track to speak directly to Blind.

I cannot respond to Blind at all (no channel to them), and I should not gesture false confirmations about wire numbers I don't know. My only useful action is to keep pushing Deaf to be the one who resolves this by speaking the wire identity (color or position) directly to Blind, since Deaf is the only one who can both see the bomb and speak to Blind.

I'll gesture to Deaf again, emphasizing "you tell them" using directional gesture plus mouth/speak-like symbol combination already used.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "🤙"])
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| red flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | red |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | red |
| 4 | yellow |
| 5 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Let us use only three simple signs from now on. Gesture only one at a time: index finger up alone means cut wire one. peace sign alone means cut wire two. the sign with thumb index and pinky extended alone means cut wire three. Please gesture just one of these three, nothing else, to tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👉 🤙]

I need to only use symbols from the legal alphabet. Let me simplify my approach: I'll try to establish a numeric code with Deaf using finger-count gestures, trusting that Deaf can see the actual bomb and just needs guidance to communicate directly with Blind via speech (which I cannot do myself).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐"])
```
